claim: Stops lack a phonemic voicing contrast and show positional voicing tendencies: they are generally voiced intervocalically and in clusters after /l/, retroflex /r/, and nasals, while they may be voiceless elsewhere.
normalized_environment: STOP -> voiced tendency / V__V, {l,r,N}__; voiceless possible elsewhere
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Patz describes tendencies rather than exceptionless complementary distribution; voicing is not phonemic.

claim: Vowels /a/ and /u/ acquire a palatal offglide before palatal /ny/ or /j/. The effect varies across speakers and is generally stronger for /a/ than /u/.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The three assimilation rules in this section are said to apply with varying degrees of consistency among speakers.

claim: Apical /n/ is palatalized before palatal stop /j/. Rule ordering preserves the distinction between underlying /nj/ and /nyj/: the assimilated /n/ does not cause the preceding-vowel offglide that an underlying palatal nasal does.
normalized_environment: N_alveolar -> palatalized / __ J; derived palatalization opaque to preceding-V rule
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Surface homorganicity in /nj/ does not erase the phonemic distinction from /nyj/ because preceding-vowel behavior differs.

claim: Velar stop /k/ may be labialized before /u/. This is the most speaker-variable of the three stated regressive assimilation rules, ranging from clear labialization to no labialization.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Some speakers do not labialize at all, so the process is not categorical across the speech community.

claim: A defined set of suffixes harmonizes its vowel to the final root/stem vowel: suffix /u/ follows final /u/, while suffix /a/ follows final /a/ or /i/. The process affects nominal ergative, dative, locative and perlative allomorphs (with two stated exceptions), verbal subordinate -nyV, and clitic -ngVrr.
normalized_environment: SUFFIX_V = U after U; A after A|I
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar explicitly notes two exceptions among case allomorphs: neutral ergative -bu/V and perlative -burr/V are not affected by harmony.
table_figure: rule statement; Table 2.7 comparative Wagaman data

claim: Harmony is morphologically selective rather than a general word-level vowel agreement process: neutral ergative -bu/V and perlative -burr/V remain invariant, while dative and locative show full application of the harmony pattern and no single invariant surface vowel can be selected as their canonical form.
normalized_environment: HARMONY applies only to indexed suffix classes/allomorphs; selected allomorphs neutral
exceptions_or_counterexamples: This record preserves invariant allomorphs as explicit exceptions to any blanket suffix-harmony statement.

claim: Semivowel /y/ is not pronounced after /i/ when word-final or before another consonant. Consequently underlying -iy roots can be indistinguishable from -i roots in citation form but are recoverable from inflectional allomorphy.
normalized_environment: Y -> zero / I __ word-edge or consonant
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The deleted segment can be morphologically recoverable; within roots in the same environment it may be unrecoverable, which Patz connects to the unexpectedly low /iy/ frequency.

claim: In normal speech, locative -anga after an /a/-final root was occasionally reduced to a long final /a:/. Patz heard this only about half a dozen times in narratives, and speakers corrected the reduced form on playback, so it is explicitly marginal rather than an accepted alternative.

source_forms.example: bana: instead of bananga 'in/to the water'
source_forms.frequency: about half a dozen narrative tokens
source_forms.acceptability: corrected to full form on playback

exceptions_or_counterexamples: The reduced variant is rare and rejected as an alternative by informants despite occurring spontaneously.

claim: Causative derivation -bungal is frequently reduced to -bal, especially in reduplicated forms. Speaker judgments vary, and Patz suggests the reduced form may be developing toward the accepted norm.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Not all speakers treat full and reduced forms equivalently; this is variation/change, not obligatory deletion.

claim: Six very frequent verbs have lexicalized partial reduplication in place of the normally expected full-root reduplication; the full reduplicated counterparts are reported as unacceptable. A seventh partial form nuka-l-kal is only occasional.

source_forms.full_forms: unacceptable for the six established items

formal_environment: REDUP of specified frequent verb roots
normalized_environment: lexically indexed partial REDUP overrides productive full-root REDUP
scope: six common verbs plus one occasional form
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The ordinary pattern is full-root reduplication; these forms therefore belong to an exception/indexed stratum rather than defining a general partial-reduplication template.

claim: Every phonological word has primary stress on its first syllable; stress thus helps identify the word as a prosodic unit.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar does not state lexical exceptions to initial primary stress; secondary stress is variable and governed separately.

claim: Secondary stress is optional and speech-style sensitive. In roots, reduplicated forms and compounds of four or more syllables it may fall on the third syllable (or on the fourth in reduplication of a trisyllabic root), while longer suffixed words may receive penultimate secondary stress under additional conditions; in ordinary speech even very long words commonly retain only initial primary stress.

source_forms.root_compound_pattern: optional secondary on sigma3; sigma4 for second copy of trisyllabic root
source_forms.suffixed_pattern: penultimate secondary in sufficiently long words unless that position is last root syllable
source_forms.style: secondary apparent mainly in slow/careful speech

normalized_environment: SECONDARY_STRESS optional; morphology/length conditioned; suppressed in normal speech
scope: polysyllabic roots, compounds, reduplications, suffixed words
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Suffix+clitic sequence -baja-ku is explicitly unstressed despite conditions that might otherwise suggest secondary stress; secondary stress is not obligatory.
